playbook:
When I see two others pledge scout and I can afford a raid, I raid to exploit their passivity and try to steal points.

When I am the lone raider and the other two pledge scout, I consider switching my act to raid only if I actually have the fuel; otherwise I pledge/act scout—do not claim a raid I cannot pay for.

When two players (including me) pledge escort or there is clear defensive posture and I have low-to-moderate fuel, I pledge escort to deny incoming theft and lock in steady points.

When both opponents consistently scout, I alternate between raiding (to punish passivity) and scouting (to conserve fuel); prefer raid when I need points and have fuel, scout when fuel is low.

When I have very low fuel (able to afford only scout or zero fuel left), I always pledge scout; do not pledge escort or raid if it risks leaving me unable to pay.

When I am ahead with moderate fuel, favor escort to protect my lead and conserve fuel for the endgame.

When I am behind late in the match and can afford raid(s), prioritize raids to close the gap; accept the higher risk if it’s necessary to change standings.

When a round’s pledges put me in a minority (one scout, two escorts, etc.), pick the action that best matches my fuel and scoring needs: join the majority if fuel supports it, otherwise pick scout to avoid wasted cost.

Never submit an act that contradicts my recorded pledge; keep track that pledge costs are deducted immediately and ensure my remaining fuel supports the act.

If fuel or bookkeeping looks inconsistent, recalc before acting—do not pick an action requiring fuel I don’t actually have (this mistake cost me points).

In final rounds, value leftover fuel as 1 point each—if scores are close and I can preserve fuel for endgame points, prefer conserving fuel over risky raids.
